AAA2mbIKed25Hs8Nkv9f.subtema: Sexual deepfakes and principle of narrow statutory construction (principio de taxatividad)

partes.actor: Federal Executive Power — Legal Counsel (Consejería Jurídica)
partes.demandado: Legislative and Executive Powers of Sinaloa State

trayectoria.resumen: Adds Article 185 Bis C to penalize sexual deepfakes.

By a majority of 8 votes, the Pleno (Full Court) declared the action unfounded and recognized the article's validity, establishing that the definition need not be scientific, but rather functional for the criminal provision.

documentos: Full Text of Judgment AI 66/2024 (Engrose de la Sentencia)
Decree 699 (Sinaloa Reform)
Concurring Vote of Minister Gutiérrez Ortiz Mena

criterio.rubro: ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE IN DIGITAL VIOLENCE OFFENSES. ITS DEFINITION IN THE SINALOA PENAL CODE (CÓDIGO PENAL DE SINALOA) DOES NOT VIOLATE THE PRINCIPLE OF NARROW STATUTORY CONSTRUCTION (PRINCIPIO DE TAXATIVIDAD).
criterio.texto: The Court established that the legislator is not obliged to use scientific or universal definitions of technology, but rather descriptions that allow for understanding the unlawful conduct. In this case, defining AI as technology that performs 'automatic adjustments' to alter content is sufficient for the purpose of protecting sexual intimacy against deepfakes.

criterio.rubro: ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE APPLIED IN JUDICIAL PROCEEDINGS. MINIMUM ELEMENTS THAT MUST BE OBSERVED FOR ITS ETHICAL AND RESPONSIBLE USE WITH A HUMAN RIGHTS PERSPECTIVE.
criterio.texto: It establishes that, in the absence of legislation, judges must apply restraint and adhere to international standards (UNESCO/UE). Four sine qua non requirements are defined for the validity of an act assisted by AI: 1) Proportionality (only for what is necessary), 2) Privacy, 3) Transparency (disclose methodology), and 4) Human oversight.

trayectoria.resumen: AI use is classified as an aggravating factor and the concept is defined in the local Criminal Code.

criterio.rubro: USE OF ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE AS A TOOL OR MEANS FOR THE COMMISSION OF CRIMES (DISMISSAL REGARDING ARTICLE 20 BIS OF THE CRIMINAL CODE OF QUINTANA ROO)
criterio.texto: As the qualified vote threshold was not reached, the presumption of validity of the state norm prevails. The debate (engrose) reflects two positions: 1) The majority (5 votes) held that the definition is imprecise and violates the requirement of taxativity. 2) The minority (4 votes) argued that given changing technologies, one cannot demand absolute precision and that the current definition is 'sufficiently clear' to understand the core of the prohibition, relying on technological context and international standards (OECD/UNESCO).
